title: Remembering Hiroshima and Nagasaki: 80 years later
description:
Join the United Nations Association of Greater Philadelphia for an engaging program to commemorate the horrors of the only time nuclear weapons were used against human beings - and for insights into the ongoing nuclear threat. 
    
This year marks 80 years since the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki — acts that reshaped history. As nuclear arsenals persist, we gather to remember, mobilize against further expansion of nuclear arsenals, and continue working for disarmament. 

Learn from peace workers, hear voices from the global community, and find out how you can join the movement to eliminate nuclear weapons.

### Speakers:
- Dr. Kathleen Welch, Back from the Brink (keynote address) 
- Dr. Christiaan Morssink, President, UNA-GP 
- Anisa Williams, Youth Speaker, CFPA 
- Shaghayegh Chris Rostampour, Physicists Coalition for Nuclear Threat Reduction

### Musical presentation:
- Cyrano Rosentrater (violin) and Alejandro Wu-Mula (piano), winners of the Jr Peace & Music Ambassador Program of Harmony for Peace Foundation. 

Networking and tabling to follow, with refreshments provided.

Please join us for a virtual phone bank ahead of our North Idaho town halls! On August 26th, we’ll be meeting at 5:30pm MT via Zoom to make phone calls to community members to invite them to upcoming town halls.

During the 2025 legislative session, Idaho lawmakers passed House Bill 93 and enacted a $50 million school-voucher program. For the first time in state history, Idaho tax dollars will be used to subsidize the cost of tuition for private-school families.

The special-interest groups promoting vouchers have made clear that the $50 million program is only the beginning. During next year’s legislative session, they intend to remove the $50-million cap and expand the program to all private-school families, including the wealthy, at an estimated cost of $339 million per year.

Such a massive expansion of vouchers would bankrupt Idaho and drain millions from public schools. For the benefit of a small number of private-school families, it would defund the public education system that serves 94% of Idaho’s kids.

It may be inevitable that the legislature tries to expand House Bill 93, but it is not inevitable that they will succeed. To stop this attack on public schools, we need to get organized. Please sign up if you can make it and we hope to see you soon!

description:
